newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Eisenberg chairman of Israel Chemicals.
newsitem.headline: Eisenberg chairman of Israel Chemicals.

text.p: The board of Israel Chemicals Ltd on Wednesday appointed Erwin Eisenberg as its chairman, replacing his late father, the billionaire Shoul Eisenberg.
Earlier this week Erwin Eisenberg was named chairman of the Israel Corp, which holds 41.9 percent of Israel Chemicals, the largest chemical group in Israel.
Erwin Eisenberg is taking over the international empire founded by his late father, who died of a heart attack in Beijing on March 27.

The younger Eisenberg, born in Japan in 1950, worked closely with his father holding various positions within the Eisenberg Group of Companies. He served as managing director of United Development Inc (UDI), the international arm of the Eisenberg Group, and was active in its operations in Asia, South America and Europe.
In 1992 he was appointed president and chief executive of the Israel Corp, one of Israel's major investment companies.

The Eisenberg Group, established over 50 years ago by Shoul Eisenberg, is involved in international projects in the areas of iron and steel, electricity generation, utilities, cement, edible oils, chemicals, textiles, shipbuilding, agriculture and water management.

The company is also active in the trade of fertilisers, steels, chemicals, tools and textiles and is involved in aircraft trading and leasing. The group's international activities are mainly done through UDI while its investments in Israel are made through the Israel Corp.
